title: 1694-physics-informed-head-impact-detection
universal_lens: Kinematic event detection via 6D acceleration tensors under binary impact classification constraints. Synthetic rare-event pretraining enables robust classifier induction via F2-optimized augmentation and time-shifted data synthesis. Universal Lens: Rooted in 1694-physics-informed-head-impact-detection (4a57d5f975630538, 3/3 pages inspected), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on 6-channel 200ms kinematic time-series using conformal prediction for real-time impact validation. Bayesian inference framework for GSI leverages synthetic priors to calibrate real-time impact detection with calibrated uncertainty estimates.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions in head impact detection using temporal convolutional kernels for event recognition and triage. GSE employs learned triggers and state transitions to dynamically route high-risk events to manual triage, optimizing workload distribution.

primitives.name: Physics-informed Machine Learning Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Sensor:** Stanford MiG2.0 mouthguard — triaxial accelerometer (±400 g @ 1000 Hz) + triaxial gyroscope (±4000 °/s @ 8000 Hz); triggers at 10 g; 200 ms windows (-50 ms pre, +150 ms post).
primitives.assumptions: Laborious manual video review as ground truth for rare event classification; physics-based synthetic data generation to augment limited real-world examples.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-class-imbalance regime (true: false ≈ 1:10) where missing true positives incurs higher cost than false alarms.

layer2.mapping: The physics-informed synthetic data augmentation addresses the same scarcity problem in GSE: how to train accurate rare-event classifiers when ground-truth labels are expensive and imbalanced. The conformal prediction framework can similarly use physics models to generate auxiliary calibration sets, reducing reliance on manual annotations.
layer2.telemetry: Classifier F2-score (weighted harmonic mean of precision and recall, β=2) as primary verification metric.

primitives.name: Finite-Element Head-Neck Impact Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: # 1694 Physics-informed ML for head impact detection (arXiv:2108.08797) **Citation:** Samuel J.
primitives.assumptions: Computational biomechanical model simulating head and neck response to external impact forces.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Generates high-fidelity synthetic impact signatures that capture complex multi-axis dynamics.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, similar physics engines simulate player trajectories and collision mechanics. These models can be inverted to generate synthetic "ground truths" for training event recognition systems, decoupling them from the bottleneck of collecting annotated match data.
layer2.telemetry: Synthetic impact dataset size and diversity serve as proxy for effective sample complexity.

primitives.name: Temporal Time-Shift Data Augmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Training strategies:** (1) field only; (2) field + 25% synthetic; (3) field + 100% synthetic; (4) pretrain on synthetic (+verified falses) then fine-tune on field; time-shift augmentation (1–5 ms, up to 5×); class-weighted loss for the 1:10 imbalance.
primitives.assumptions: Impact events are translationally invariant in time within a small window; temporal jitter does not alter the underlying physical cause.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mitigates overfitting to the specific timing artifacts of real sensors while preserving event structure.

layer2.mapping: Time-shift augmentation mirrors the spatio-temporal data augmentation used in GSE for tracking data, where player poses are permuted to learn equivariant representations. It also relates to conformal prediction's need for exchangeable out-of-sample tests.
layer2.telemetry: Number of augmented samples per epoch tracks effective regularization strength.

primitives.name: F2-Score Evaluation Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Callan, Eli Rice, Yuzhe Liu, Zhou Zhou, Michael Zeineh, David B.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_beta': 'Dimensionless F-measure', 'beta': 'Weight parameter (typically 1 for balanced error, 2 for recall-heavy)', 'precision': 'True positives / (true positives + false positives)', 'recall': 'True positives / (true positives + false negatives)'}
primitives.assumptions: Precision-recall tradeoff modeled as a weighted harmonic mean; fixed misclassification costs encoded in beta.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Recall-oriented optimization where false negatives dominate the objective function.

layer2.mapping: The F2-score maps directly to GSI's need for high sensitivity in anomaly detection (e.g., identifying unusual betting patterns). In GSE, it could measure injury-event recall while controlling false alarm rates.
layer2.telemetry: F2-score computed on independent test set serves as out-of-bag performance estimate.

primitives.name: Feature Space Definition

layer2.mapping: Dataset partitioning mirrors GSI’s stratified sampling protocol for robust statistical inference.
